title: Operate, Optimize, and the Reference Architecture: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Operate, Optimize, and the Reference Architecture: Visual Guide

1. From Design To Operations | the producers-to-consumers strip built entirely from lessons 01-07 (Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, Dataflow, BigQuery, IAM, CMEK, Dataplex, orchestrator), with a switch between 'as designed' and 'as operated' and five failure questions you can fire at either version | the same boxes answer 0 of 5 failure questions as designed and 5 of 5 once dead-letter paths, dedup at retry boundaries, quality gates, monitoring and a recovery plane are drawn, so the operational layer is what turns a logo collage into an architecture

2. Impact To Cause | four scenarios (late data, quality drift, complete outage, transient retries) lighting up the three dashboard layers, plus a slider for how long impact must be sustained before anyone is paged | monitoring the consumer objective first walks a responder from impact to stage to resource, and requiring ~5 minutes of sustained impact drops 84 noise pages a week while still catching both real incidents with 35 minutes of runway before the 07:00 deadline

3. Where The Money Went | two incidents in one panel - a bill split into volume, unit price and efficiency sliders with an idle-cluster toggle against an 8,000 TB / $5 per TB / $40,000 baseline, and a 100 req/s quota storm where 1,000 clients retry on a fixed 5-second timer or with bounded backoff plus jitter | cost per processed TB is the useful unit that separates growth (volume up, unit cost flat) from a defect (a regressed partition filter or an idle cluster), and synchronized retries turn a quota failure into the outage while jitter drains the same queue in two rounds

4. Idle Or Waiting | jobs-per-day and minutes-per-job sliders comparing 24 billed hours on a persistent Dataproc cluster against ephemeral clusters paying ~90 seconds of creation per job, plus four tappable pieces of state that decide whether the workflow is disposable at all | four 40-minute batch jobs a day is 11% utilization so ephemeral wins, sixty three-minute jobs make startup a 33% tax so persistent wins - but if inputs, outputs, checkpoints, code or metadata live on cluster disk the economics do not get a vote

5. RPO, RTO, Restore | three failure types (region outage, corruption from a bad deploy, deletion) sorting five defences into HELPS and NO HELP, with a snapshot-interval slider converting the interval into an RPO and into events lost at 3,000 events per minute | replication is not a backup - it copies corruption and deletion faithfully - and RPO (data loss in time) is not RTO (time to restore), with 15-minute snapshots meaning up to 45,000 events at risk
